Sessions / Session 04 Day 4

Session 04 — Day 4: Pre-Raid

Second Finestra day. The raid fires tomorrow. Today the city is being tuned: false alarms conditioning the crowd, final handler deployment, Slaad pre-positioned. The party does not know any of this unless they have been pulling threads. Today is the last day they can act before the operation runs.

Dawn — What Changed Overnight

ThreadState at dawn
RaidDay 4 of prep. Final handler deployment. All five extraction paths confirmed and clear. Slaad materials in final position. Purple-caste raid teams en route to the city via the vethka. Tomorrow is the strike.
BeffaSecond Finestra day. More pranks, more false alarms. The crowd’s hesitation reflex is sharpening — they have been trained to laugh first and look second.
Red LadyCommission clock: 3–5 days. The sealed chart package has been collected. Crew arriving in Calveno today and tomorrow.
ShipDay 4 of ~5. If the party hasn’t given Sem a plate decision yet, he finds them this morning (see below). If they already decided, he’s installing their choice.
PearlIf the Summons fired: the demand is two days old. Delmar has refused but the Pearl is still in the wreck. If not: Branca is in the shrine for the fifth dawn. The shrine has become a minor public curiosity.
WarrenIf JC went underground: the Warren has sealed one or two tunnel access points. If not: those lanes are open.
DM Note

Today is the decision day. Whatever the party has learned, whatever they’ve ignored — the state of the board at sundown tonight determines what the raid looks like tomorrow. Don’t rush them. Let them make choices that feel consequential because they are.

Registry Plate — Sem’s Deadline (Conditional)

Skip if the party already made this decision.

If the registry plate is still undecided, Sem finds whoever is responsible for the ship — at their lodging, the dock, or the street.

Read Aloud

Sem is standing outside the Ponte Bassa with sawdust in his beard and a piece of brass plate under one arm. He does not sit down. “Hull’s done tomorrow. I need a name for the bow or I’m sending her out blank. Crown plate’s still bolted on. Your call — keep it, scrape it, or tell me what goes in its place. I need the answer by tonight.”

DM Note

If Delmar isn’t there, Sem finds Perrin — “Your ship, your crew’s problem.” The three options and consequences are in Day 3. Let them discuss and decide. Sem nods once and leaves.

Handler Cell — Combat

Jean-Claude (primary), anyone he brings. Combat-ready encounter.

If JC has been following the handler thread — Day 2 recognition beats, Day 3 tunnel investigation — today he can confront a handler cell directly. This is the escalation point.

Setup

JC spots what looks like operational handler work — a pair of Grung in nondescript trade clothes at the same Bridge pillar he clocked on Day 2, different position, same posture. Not watching the performer. Watching the crowd move around the performer. The hour is wrong for the spot.

Read Aloud

Two figures in trade clothes at the same Bridge pillar Jean-Claude clocked two days ago — different position now, same posture. They are not watching the performer. They are watching the crowd move around the performer. The hour is wrong for the spot.

The Fight

Location: Le Paludi — narrow canal, 5 ft alleys, two boats tied at the nearest mooring. Poor light. Festival crowd two streets over.

Tactical Map — Handler Alley

Mechanic

Blue-Caste Handler x 2. Scout stats (MM p.349). AC 13, HP 16. Shortbow +4, 1d8+3 piercing + Grung Poison (DC 11 Con save or poisoned 1 min). Standing Leap 20 ft as part of movement. Breaks and runs at half HP — they have a report to file.

Tactics: break contact first. Fight only if cornered. One draws pursuit down the alley while the other cuts through a boat mooring. If one escapes, they report. If both escape, Simone learns the party is in Calveno and JC’s face is now a priority.

DM Note

Scaling. If the party has magic weapons or high-AC frontliners, add a third handler — a spotter on a rooftop with a hand crossbow, same stats. The encounter should feel fast and breakable. If it lasts more than four rounds, the handlers disengage and flee underground. This is a skirmish, not a boss fight.

What the Handlers Carry

One handler has:

  • Binding rope — light, professional, pre-knotted
  • Sealed wax message cylinder — blank on inspection, but the wax bears a mark Jean-Claude recognizes from Botukuri shipping labels
DM Note

Three outcomes, all real: Capture alive: the handler knows arrival timing and the extraction canal route. Telling the Warren closes one of five lanes. The handler also knows the vethka position and can confirm the Dravosi patrol gap — giving the party the full operational picture for the first time. Kill both: one lane goes dark. Simone doesn’t learn the cell was made. The raid loses one strike point without explanation. Let them go: Simone learns the party is in Calveno. JC’s face is now a report. The raid proceeds at full strength with the additional knowledge that the Blue Grung Deserter is in the city.

If JC Doesn’t Engage

The handler cell completes its final route confirmation. All five lanes are open and timed. Tomorrow’s raid proceeds at full capacity. No combat, no intelligence, no consequence today — but the absence of action is the consequence.

Red Lady — The Convergence

Delmar (primary), Crissdalynn. The vise tightens.

By Day 4, three threads are pointing at the same wreck. Let the party feel the pressure without narrating the connection for them.

ThreadWhat it says
Umberlee’s demandRetrieve the Pearl from the Red Lady wreck. Return it to a shrine. The reward is Delmar’s death.
Salvage commissionA funded crew is 3–5 days from departing Calveno for the same wreck. Better equipped, better charted.
Kyzil’s phrase”Your ship didn’t go down to weather, Priscilla.” The Red Lady is both Delmar’s wreck and part of Crissdalynn’s past.

The Offer

Delmar counts as “visible” if he: (a) asked Zusto about salvage, (b) asked a chandler about Maw gear, or (c) was mentioned by name to anyone at the Bridge. If none of these happened, the runner doesn’t come — the commission departs without him. This is the world moving, not a punishment.

Read Aloud

A runner from the Bridge finds Delmar at the Ponte Bassa. Clean clothes, damp hair, a polite voice that does not carry. “My employer heard there’s a captain in Calveno who’s actually sailed the Maw. Not many of those. He’d like to talk. No obligation. He’s buying.”

DM Note

The offer is genuine. The commission’s operational lead wants Maw navigation expertise and is willing to pay for it. The terms are: retained navigator on the salvage expedition, standard crew share of recovered cargo, departure in 3–5 days. The trap is structural, not personal — joining the commission puts Delmar inside the operation that’s racing him to the Pearl. Don’t spring it as a betrayal. Let it sit as a complicated offer the party has to discuss.

If ignored: the commission doesn’t need him. They have charts. The lugger departs on schedule and reaches the Maw ahead of the party.

False Alarms — Crowd Conditioning

Ambient. Drop these into scenes the party is already in — one at midday crowd peak, one at the watch shift change.

The Beffa is doing its work. The crowd has been trained.

Midday — Mercatura crowd peak:

Read Aloud

A scream cuts across the Mercatura — high, sharp, genuine terror. The crowd freezes for one breath. Then someone sees the mask, and the laughter starts. A Beffa team has staged a mugging with fake blood and a victim who falls too theatrically. The crowd claps. The mark — who was the victim — takes a bow. Everyone relaxes.

DM Note

This is the conditioning the raid depends on. Tomorrow, the first screams during the real operation will buy three to five seconds of crowd hesitation — people looking for the mask, waiting for the punchline, before they understand that the thing happening in front of them is not a performance. That delay is the operational gap. Let the party see the training happening. Don’t explain what it’s for.

Watch shift change — harbour approach:

Read Aloud

Three figures in half-masks sprint past the harbour approach and vault a canal railing — Beffa runners, mid-prank, pursued by a furious mark with wine-stained trousers. The watch at the canal gate watches them pass without moving. The gate sergeant shakes his head.

The watch is not going to respond to screams during festival week unless someone makes them. Their intervention threshold is higher than it will be on any other week of the year. The raid planners know this.

Grung desensitization — final beat: a Velo mask vendor is doing brisk trade in “Grung masks” — green, wide-mouthed, painted with caste colours. A group of festival-goers in Grung masks runs through the Mercatura shrieking and pretending to snatch each other. The crowd claps. Tomorrow, when real Grung emerge from the ground, the first three seconds of the crowd’s response will be applause.

Beffa Play — Day 4

If the party has a registered team: second Finestra day. Two days left in the execution window. If they haven’t struck yet, the pressure is building — their mark knows they’re coming but not when.

Ambient scoring: two more pranks scored today. One Legendary entry fails spectacularly and provides table comedy. Moretti is still untouched — the committee is starting to wonder if anyone will even try this year.

Raid Prep Status Check

DM reference only. Assess the board at end of day.

The raid fires tomorrow (Beffa Day 4 / party Day 5). The party’s actions over Days 1–4 determine what state it’s in.

ElementFully intactPartially disruptedFully disrupted
Extraction lanes (5)All five sewer routes open and timed1–2 routes sealed via Warren; 3–4 remainAll five sealed (requires extraordinary party action)
Handler networkAll cells operational1 cell destroyed or captured; Simone alerted or notMultiple cells made; network compromised
Slaad pre-positioningIn place, ready for distraction deploymentDelayed if handlers were disrupted on Day 3+Intercepted only if the party found the staging area
Crowd conditioningFestival has trained perfect hesitationUnchanged — the Beffa did this, not the handlersCannot be disrupted; it’s civic behavior
Dravosi patrol gapScheduled and holdingUnchanged — this is real naval schedulingCould be closed only if the party warned a Dravosi authority
DM Note

The party cannot stop the raid entirely within the scope of Session 04. They can reduce its scale. Each extraction lane sealed removes one strike point. Each handler captured gives the Warren intelligence to pre-position responders. A fully disrupted raid (3+ lanes closed, handler network compromised) becomes a chaotic partial operation that the city can survive — dozens taken instead of hundreds. A fully intact raid is a watershed. Either result changes the world.

Night Before the Storm

DM Note

Spotlight. JC owns the handler cell if he engages. Delmar owns the Red Lady offer if it fires. The registry plate belongs to whoever cares about the ship. Make sure each player has one moment today where the table is listening to them.

If the party has assembled the picture: they know an organized Grung operation is running through Calveno’s sewers, timed to the festival. They may know the scale (five strikes), the extraction method (sewer to outer water), and the pickup (vethka past the patrol minimum). They have options: warn the Warren, warn the watch, position themselves at a known strike point, seal more lanes, pursue the vethka.

If the party hasn’t assembled the picture: they sleep. Tomorrow is the last day of La Finestra. The committee is preparing Il Giudizio scoring. The city is relaxed, amused, a little drunk. The crowd will hesitate.

Read Aloud

The canal is quiet. Lanterns hang from mooring posts, their reflections broken by the slow push of the tide. Somewhere in the Velo a bodhran is playing, and from the Mercatura the sound of the committee setting up the scoring stage for tomorrow’s Il Giudizio. The city is warm, fed, and a little drunk. It has no idea.

DM Note

Don’t tell the party what they missed. If they go to bed without acting on the handler thread, that is a valid outcome — the raid’s scale is the consequence, not a punishment. If they’ve been focused on the Pearl, the ship, the Warren, the Beffa — those are real choices with real payoffs. The raid is what moves when they look away.

Day Close — Setting Up Tomorrow

ThreadState at sundown
RaidAll prep complete. Purple-caste raid teams are in the city. Five strike points manned. Slaad release materials staged. Vethka at anchor past the patrol line. The operation fires at tomorrow’s crowd peak.
Red LadyCommission clock: 2–4 days. Crew assembled in Calveno. Departure preparation underway.
ShipDay 4 of ~5. Registry plate installed (whichever option they chose). Tomorrow is the last day of hull work.
BeffaSecond Finestra day complete. Il Giudizio scoring prep begins. Tomorrow is the last execution day — and the raid’s cover.

Tomorrow — The Raid

The raid fires on Day 5 (Beffa Day 4, the last day of La Finestra). Full Day 5 content is ready: Day 5 — The Raid.

If the table reaches Day 5, you have:

  • Calveno — Beffa Grung Raid — full operational plan: blackpowder detonation, five strike points, Slaad summoning, sewer extraction, purple-caste handlers
  • Slaad boss encounter — Red Slaad stat block, environment, tactics, scaling notes
  • Secondary strike encounters — read-aloud and stat blocks for each site
  • Nona’s aftermath — her speech, the Passage’s public alliance with Calveno, pursuit assembly
  • Raid scale — based on tonight’s status check
